title: Showing Ownership with -s and til
goal: Use Norwegian -s and til patterns to show who owns or is connected to something.

objectives.statement: Use Norwegian -s and til patterns to show who owns or is connected to something.

sections.title: A key, a bag, and several moving boxes

spans.value: Jonas is helping Nora move into a new apartment. Nora’s brother Emil has also brought some boxes, but nobody has labeled everything clearly.
Hvor er nøkkelen til leiligheten?

blocks.translation: Where is the key to the apartment?

spans.value: Den ligger kanskje i Emils sekk.

blocks.translation: It may be in Emil’s backpack.

spans.value: Nei, dette er Jonas’ sekk. Sekken min står ved døra.

blocks.translation: No, this is Jonas’s backpack. My backpack is by the door.

spans.value: Vent litt. Er dette nøkkelen til Nora?

blocks.translation: Wait a moment. Is this Nora’s key?

spans.value: Ja, det er leilighetens nøkkel. Flott!

blocks.translation: Yes, it is the apartment’s key. Great!

spans.value: Og hvor skal Noras bøker stå?

blocks.translation: And where should Nora’s books go?

spans.value: I bokhylla til Jonas. Han har lånt meg den.

blocks.translation: In Jonas’s bookcase. He has lent it to me.

spans.value: Men eskene til Emil kan stå på kjøkkenet.

blocks.translation: But Emil’s boxes can go in the kitchen.

spans.value: The three speakers need to identify people’s belongings and explain how objects are connected. Norwegian commonly does this in two ways:

items.value: to the owner or other connecting noun;
after the person or thing being identified.

spans.value: These patterns can often express the same basic relationship:
The meaning is similar, but the order and form of the nouns change.

sections.title: First notice: Who or what is connected to whom?

spans.value: In a phrase such as Noras bøker, Nora is the person connected to the books. In bøkene til Nora, the same two parts appear in the opposite order.
Owner or connection first; thing first

“Owner” is a convenient word, but these patterns are not limited to literal ownership. A person can own a bag, but an apartment does not own its key in the same way. The pattern also shows a close connection.
In each case, ask two simple questions:

items.value: What person or thing are we identifying?
Who or what is it connected to?

spans.value: In nøkkelen til leiligheten, we are identifying nøkkelen, and it is connected to leiligheten.
To use the
-s pattern
, put the owner or connecting noun first and add
-s
directly to it.
Compact rule:
There is normally no apostrophe before the
s
The English translation uses an apostrophe, but ordinary Norwegian
-s
does not.
Form of the thing after -s
After an
-s
owner, the thing normally appears without a definite ending. Compare:
The owner already tells us which book, bicycle, or room we mean. Norwegian therefore does not normally use the definite form of the second noun in this pattern.
A common mistake is to keep that definite ending:
This is not the standard pattern. Use:
The same point applies in the plural:
Norwegian can also put the thing first and introduce the owner or connection with
til
Compact rule:

statement.value: definite thing + til + owner or connection

spans.value: Notice that the first noun is normally definite:
This contrasts directly with the
-s
pattern:
Do not copy English word order mechanically. Norwegian does not normally use an indefinite form of the thing for this possessive meaning. When
til
identifies whose particular object you mean, use the definite form of the thing:

en.value: book to Nora (for the possessive meaning)

spans.value: That last phrase may suggest a book intended for Nora rather than a book connected to or belonging to her. The definite form helps produce the intended ownership reading.
Both patterns are common:
The
-s
pattern is short and places the owner or connection first. It works especially neatly with names and short nouns:
The
til
pattern places the object first. This is useful when the object is already central to the conversation or when you ask which person it is connected to:
The
til
pattern can also feel convenient when the connecting phrase is longer:
At this level, the main goal is not to identify a subtle stylistic difference. It is to form both patterns naturally and understand that they can describe the same relationship.
Same situation, different starting point
Imagine that Nora sees a coat and wants to know whose it is. She can receive either answer:
The first answer begins with Emil. The second begins with the jacket. Both identify the same connection.
Likewise:

en.value: This is the entrance to the building.

spans.value: The second version may be especially natural when someone is looking for an entrance and inngangen is the topic. The grammar does not change the basic relationship.
The same patterns show family, institutional, and part–whole connections.
People and relationships
These people are connected through a relationship; nobody is being treated as an object that someone owns.
Places and their parts
Organizations and information
The same core question remains useful: What are we identifying, and what is it connected to?
After carrying the boxes upstairs, Nora, Jonas, and Emil try to put everything in the right place.
Er dette Emils lampe?
Nei, lampa til Emil er svart. Det er min lampe.

blocks.translation: No, Emil’s lamp is black. That is my lamp.

spans.value: Jeg har funnet beina til bordet, men hvor er bordets skruer?

blocks.translation: I have found the table legs, but where are the table’s screws?

spans.value: Skruene til bordet ligger i den lille eska.

blocks.translation: The table’s screws are in the small box.

spans.value: Og dette må være naboens post.

blocks.translation: And this must be the neighbor’s mail.

spans.value: Ja. Posten til naboen skal ikke ligge her. Jeg går ned med den.

blocks.translation: Yes. The neighbor’s mail should not be here. I’ll take it downstairs.

spans.value: The speakers move freely between the two patterns:

items.value: Emils lampe and lampa til Emil
bordets skruer and skruene til bordet
naboens post and posten til naboen

spans.value: Each pair preserves the same connection while changing which part comes first.
